description: WHEN OTHER of 9200-GETCARDXREF-BYACCT at :759-766, the third and last arm of the EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :737, whose WHEN order - NORMAL at :738, NOTFND at :741, OTHER at :759 - is preserved exactly (gate G30). case08 drives the NOTFND arm of this same site from seeded rows, so this file drives the OTHER arm and only that arm; the two do not overlap. The site is the CXACAIX PATH over the CCXREF base, reached through the one CardXrefRepository's alternate-key finder readByAccountIdViaAltIndex and never through a second repository or a second table (gate G45) - a rule that holds on the failure path exactly as it does on the success path. CCXREF is declared empty and the forced outcome is applied to the read of the empty dataset, which is what names one of three identically keyed READ sites; the other two datasets still hold their rows, so the flow still reaches the site being driven, and no seeded row could produce this arm anyway. The two response codes are not case data and cannot drift: the repository answers ReadResult.other(CXACAIX, PERMANENT_ERROR_STATUS), which carries FileStatus.NOTOPEN = 19 and CardXrefRepository.CICS_RESP2_NOT_APPLICABLE = 0, both compile-time constants, so the composed text is identical on every run (practice B7). WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE is built at :86-105 from nine spans summing to exactly 80: FILLER X(12) 'File Error: ', ERROR-OPNAME X(8) holding 'READ', FILLER X(4) ' on ', ERROR-FILE X(9) holding LIT-CARDXREFNAME-ACCT-PATH, which is PIC X(8) VALUE 'CXACAIX ' at :192-193 so its trailing space is part of the value, FILLER X(15) ' returned RESP ', ERROR-RESP X(10), FILLER X(7) ',RESP2 ', ERROR-RESP2 X(10), and a closing FILLER X(5) of spaces. ERROR-RESP and ERROR-RESP2 are PIC X(10) receiving PIC S9(09) COMP, so each renders as nine digits left justified with one pad space: '000000019 ' and '000000000 '. MOVE WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE TO WS-RETURN-MSG at :766 then truncates the 80-character group into PIC X(75), losing exactly the closing five-space FILLER and nothing else, and :532 moves that into ERRMSGO PIC X(78), which re-pads by three. The early exit is the second thing this case pins. The arm sets FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK at :761, so the guard at :696-699 - whose original condition on :696 is commented out in favour of the flag test on :697 - fires, and 9300-GETACCTDATA-BYACCT and 9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST are never performed. That forward-only GO TO is a plain return with its evaluation order and fall-through outcome intact (rule R7). ACCTDAT and CUSTDAT are seeded with account 00000000050 and customer 000000050 and are expected byte-for-byte unchanged, yet every account and customer field on the painted screen is LOW-VALUES, including the five numeric-edited money items, because 1200 populates them only under FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER or FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER at :471-522 and neither flag was ever set. That absence is the proof: had either read run, those fields would carry data. 1200 takes its ELSE at :464 with FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK false, so :468 echoes the typed CC-ACCT-ID into ACCTSIDO. 1300 colours the field at :555-559 - DFHDFCOL first, then DFHRED because FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK - while the asterisk at :561-565 stays away because it needs FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK: red without the marker, which is FieldAttributeSetter's rule, implemented inline here because COACTVWC does not copy CSSETATY. INFOMSGC is DFHNEUTR rather than DFHBMDAR because :528-530 flipped WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE, set at :689, to WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT before :567-571 tested it, which is also why INFOMSGO carries the 39-character prompt of :113-114 padded through PIC X(40) to PIC X(45). The program writes nothing - its only file verbs are the three EXEC CICS READs at :727, :776 and :826 - so expectedWrites is empty and the return code is 0. Every expected value here is statically derived from the COBOL, from CVACT03Y's 50-byte layout, from the symbolic map's xxxI PICTURE clauses and from the real app/data/ASCII fixtures; none of it was captured from a live COBOL execution, which this environment cannot run (risk R-A). The fixtures were measured for this case: all 50 cross-reference rows are 36 bytes and their XREF-ACCT-ID span at offset 25 covers exactly accounts 00000000001 through 00000000050, so a genuine cross-reference miss needs either a curated window, which is what case08 uses, or an out-of-range id such as 00000000099, which the fixture does not contain - and neither of those produces this arm, which is why this one is forced. WHICH READ IS DRIVEN, DECLARED RATHER THAN INFERRED: the forcedOutcomes member above is keyed by repository operation, and all three of COACTVWC's file verbs are READ - the EXEC CICS READs of CXACAIX at :787, ACCTDAT at :843 and CUSTDAT at :864 - so the key alone cannot say which of them reports the outcome. It used to be INFERRED from whichever dataset this file happened to declare empty, which was a sound rule but a convention: a reader could not see which read was driven without knowing the rule and cross-checking three inputs entries, and no case could drive a read of a dataset that still held rows. unitStimulus.callSiteOutcomes now NAMES the site, once, in the same file as the expectation that depends on it. The old rule survives as a required cross-check rather than as the decision: the named site must also be this case's one empty dataset - an empty dataset is one whose rows cannot answer any key, which is exactly why the outcome must be supplied rather than seeded, and because the other two still hold their rows the reads before it still succeed and the flow still reaches the site being driven. Two declarations that disagree are refused rather than one being quietly honoured.
